principles.statement: Start from the product problem and intended outcome before proposing initiatives.
Separate outputs, outcomes and impacts explicitly.
Treat strategy as choices and exclusions, not a list of initiatives.
Preserve evidence provenance and label assumptions, unknowns and contradictions.
Do not infer authority from evidence, recommendations or framework output.
Prioritization must expose criterion, ordering, trade-offs and excluded work.
Choose only context-relevant frameworks and record why alternatives were rejected.
Avoid false precision when evidence cannot support numeric confidence or forecasts.
Closed tasks and binding obligations stay closed unless new authority explicitly reopens them.
Candidate value is established through comparative evidence, not asserted by the package.
